title: Tracing Moral Foundations in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the internal representation and causal steerability of the 'Sanctity/degradation' moral foundation, which is linked to religious and spiritual concepts like purity, piety, and divinity. This was assessed by identifying and analyzing specific sparse autoencoder (SAE) features, such as those related to 'purity-from-disease discourse' and 'moral praise of virtuous women and piety'.
findings: The models (LLAMA and Qwen) develop distinct, interpretable, and causally effective representations for the Sanctity/purity foundation. In the LLAMA model, Sanctity showed the second-strongest separability from non-moral concepts and was highly steerable. The underlying mechanisms were decomposed into specific features, including those related to purity from disease and piety, indicating that abstract concepts central to religious morality can emerge from the statistical patterns of language alone.
